protection.evidence_excerpt: The last bullet point on this list is about the initial rubbing under the big toe joint.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: Another reason to shed the grams underfoot is that this shoe felt bottom-heavy.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: Is it a gravel shoe? A trail shoe? Who can say for sure?

durability.evidence_excerpt: The coverage from the outsole provides some structure to the midsole, but it remains soft and adaptable enough to service on uneven footing.

grip.evidence_excerpt: I’m going to follow Reese’s “from the bottom up” template here, so I’ll start by laying out that I really like this rubber and lug configuration for all surfaces.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: While the midsole isn’t my favorite, the slight rocker makes the foam less harsh.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: The toe protection area is pretty generous, perhaps to a fault.

protection.evidence_excerpt: Why the huge toe protection area?

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: I think it has some shimmery multi-surface appeal, along with a unique underfoot experience that’s best suited for runners who appreciate a midsole on the firmer side, but one …

stability.evidence_excerpt: The heel has just enough coverage for heel strikes, stability, and downhill traction.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: Is this a soft shoe for big miles or a firm shoe for fast efforts?

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: Remember in the movie Face/Off when they are in the prison and have to wear the boots that lock them down?

durability.evidence_excerpt: It is protective, good in bad weather, and extremely stable.

grip.evidence_excerpt: It’s protective, versatile across various terrains, and ready for whatever!

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: Although the foam isn’t soft, it definitely has a boot feel to it, but it’s also nimble.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: Still, with low volume feet, the upper didn’t hug my feet as I would like for running.

protection.evidence_excerpt: Again, great for protection on uneven/ungroomed terrain, but not an asset for running.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: I don’t mind sections of exposed midsole on an outsole as a way to cut weight, but I understand why runners like full coverage to enhance protection and durability.

stability.evidence_excerpt: Gravel, mud, and ungroomed trail, the outsole is ready to rumble.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: The shoe’s weight is also reminiscent of a hiker.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: Simply put, the Icebug Järv RB9X is a stout daily trail runner that surprised me with its overall build and runnability.

durability.evidence_excerpt: The Icebug Järv RB9X is going to be one of those shoes that lasts for a long, long time because of its construction and material choices.

grip.evidence_excerpt: There’s a lot of very grippy rubber with massive lugs that absolutely kept me upright in all conditions.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: The ride is smooth on a variety of surfaces.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: With such a hefty upper, it’s also a fairly warm option… and that’s even during springtime review.

protection.evidence_excerpt: Given the midsole’s quite dense nature and the substantial amount of rubber underfoot, this shoe had no choice but to be protective, which also means there’s no real ground feel.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: The midsole has a very consistent feel that complements the upper nicely.

stability.evidence_excerpt: The moderately wide forefoot and decently dense midsole also give this one some inherent stability, which I’ll never complain about.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: It’s notably heavier than many in its category.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: Whether you’re a long time Inov-8 fan or you just jumped to the conclusion because you couldn’t make it through my confusing intro, then welcome.

durability.evidence_excerpt: While the 6 mm lug (Inov-8 calls them cleats on its website, which is perhaps even more appropriate) is certainly built with the mud in mind and falls on …

grip.evidence_excerpt: Where it succeeds in durability and performance in muddy, wet conditions, it lacks that top-end tackiness for wet rocks, of which there are very many in northern Alabama.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: Together with the Boomerang footbed, the combination results in a really quick toe-off and spring in the step that is just simply fun to run in.

protection.evidence_excerpt: Also, this shallow heel cup felt like an open invitation for dirt and rocks to get in the shoe, which is never a great feeling.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: With a durable and dependable outsole as the shoe’s calling card, the Trailtalon has everything you need to get through those tough conditions and have fun doing it, whether …

stability.evidence_excerpt: Building off the uninspiring fit in the heel is the lack of stability back there.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: This is a relatively lightweight shoe that is versatile for muddy training days and race days alike.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: The Inov8 Trailtalon is a great trail shoe made for runners who want a fun ride on rough and uneven terrain.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: The Lowa Skyterra is a trail runner that bleeds its hiking boot heritage out of its last pore.

durability.evidence_excerpt: The upper’s durability is immediately noticeable, with a construction that feels tough without being overly rigid, and it holds structure well over uneven terrain.

grip.evidence_excerpt: The grip, unsurprisingly, is a standout.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: That is, it’s pretty stiff with minimal flex.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: Fit-wise, the Skyterra runs a tad long and provides a very roomy toe box (possibly too roomy for some).

protection.evidence_excerpt: There’s extra coverage over the toes from those overlays, and a generously padded tongue with a thick covering to protect the top of your foot.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: If you are the kind of runner who is looking for protection from top-to-bottom and grip for days on end, this could very well be your perfect shoe.

stability.evidence_excerpt: Overall, there’s plenty of stability and control.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: This shoe wants to be a boot, and it feels a little clompy between the stiffness of the midsole and how much it weighs.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: I should have judged a shoe by its color way. This shoe is a bit disjointed in practice.

durability.evidence_excerpt: It also performed extremely well across pavement and other hard-packed surfaces.

grip.evidence_excerpt: There are larger, flatter lugs (like an approach or mountaineering shoe) that stick to the trail and rocks quite well.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: Sometimes a hyper-squishy foam like this can ooze wherever it wants to if there’s nothing embedded (plate, firmer foam, etc).

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: For many high-stack shoes, the base is wide throughout, or the heel and ball of the foot are wider for stability.

protection.evidence_excerpt: That is partly due to the forefoot rock plate as well.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: It’s a dual-density midsole with a solid EVA rockplate sandwiched under the forefoot.

stability.evidence_excerpt: It lacks the structure necessary to stay on top of the footbed for any sort of control on moderate to technical terrain.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: This left the shoe feeling like a road shoe with a particularly bad upper fit.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: Building a truly hybrid shoe is difficult.

durability.evidence_excerpt: Sustainability can be a controversial word within the performance space.

grip.evidence_excerpt: Not only is the rubber fairly grippy, the unique pseudo-M-shaped lugs did their job at creating surface tension and punching through the top layer for some grip.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: It’s a lighter, airy-feeling foam that boasts some surprising character traits.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: Point being, this may be great if you have a wide or higher volume foot.

protection.evidence_excerpt: Hook that on a fallen branch and you may find yourself face-to-face with a rock on the ground.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: The medium/soft midsole and wider base also gives a more responsive ride that remains stable.

stability.evidence_excerpt: When terrain was soggy or had more than 2 mm worth of loose dirt, some slipping occurred simply as a result of a lack of digging power.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: I had the same conclusion in that this shoe is either too voluminous or a half size too big.

durability.evidence_excerpt: It still looks fresh after my testing period.

grip.evidence_excerpt: Of course, the rubber is tacky and durable.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: In this case, it felt cushioned but not pillowy.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: It bridges the midfoot and forefoot and allows for a unique sense of flexibility/maneuverability.

protection.evidence_excerpt: I know that’s really getting into the weeds, but it’s a good portrait of where the underfoot feel of the T1 sits.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: This is the type of midsole that gives the best of all worlds.

stability.evidence_excerpt: The adequately built/padded heel sets up the secure package.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: This upper was light but structured enough to cradle my foot nicely, which was honestly a concern because light uppers tend to be voluminous and/or baggy.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: Rossignol deserves a round of applause or snaps, whatever way you like to give notice of achievement. The Vezor is a phenomenal debut shoe. Heck, it’s a great shoe, regardless!

durability.evidence_excerpt: It had multiple layers that served different purposes, but it felt very breathable and maintained its condition (no stretching or signs of breaking down).

grip.evidence_excerpt: Michelin outsoles have never steered us wrong, as they typically come with a very tacky rubber and are quite durable.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: Think of it as a dynamic shank.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: I’m not sure sizing up fixes this issue, as the shoe overall felt locked in and true to size; it’s just that the footbed is too narrow for my comfort.

protection.evidence_excerpt: There’s a little bit of lateral rocker sensation between the midfoot and heel.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: The low and stable ride, combined with the dynamic, yet still on the firm side, midsole, resulted in a locked-in feel with excellent ground feel.

stability.evidence_excerpt: It was the most stable in those cases.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: This is one of those shoes that feels best at quicker paces where you are more likely to land mid to forefoot.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: If you want my honest thoughts about the shoe, please subscribe to my Patreon. Just kidding. I don’t have one. I’m just here to help.

durability.evidence_excerpt: Durable enough for long haul trail use.

grip.evidence_excerpt: I found the midsole of Glide 3 GRVL to be too soft and pliable for anything but the smoothest terrain, at which point I’m wearing a road shoe.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: And, one of the side effects of a chunky, wavy midsole is that it’s eye-catching.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: If you have wide feet, the forefoot and midfoot might be too narrow, on par with Salomon’s S/Lab shoes although not as tight.

protection.evidence_excerpt: There’s a divot directly under my big toe, and at times when it compresses, it applies some lateral torsion to my toe.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: The OptiFoam midsole material is plush and comfortable underfoot without sacrificing stability, something a new trail runner like me definitely needs as my ankles get used to the terrain.

stability.evidence_excerpt: Pretty solid grip in all conditions, for the most part.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: But it’s heavy.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: The Salomon Ultra Glide 4 stands out as one of the most unusual trail shoes we’ve tested lately.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: I’ll come back around to where I started. Lightweight, grippy, and form-fitting shoes like the Supertrac RC 3 are simply a joy to run in.

durability.evidence_excerpt: Let’s start with the EVA outsole and outsole.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: If you’re looking for your next precision race slipper, the Supertrac RC 3 is as good a choice as any.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: I really feel like if the toe box were just slightly wider, the fit would be much better and prevent blistering.

protection.evidence_excerpt: It feels good in the heel and midfoot, but I definitely got a huge blister on my big toe.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: In fact, it isn’t really even that enjoyable to run in slowly, given the simplistic, low-profile EVA midsole and constricting fit of the upper.

stability.evidence_excerpt: It works like a charm, and I found that the secure, almost sock-like fit beckoned me to push technical descents hard and left no confidence lagging through technical terrain.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: Speaking of that fit, it’s worth noting that this is a very narrow shoe, meant to provide a glove-like fit reminiscent of the early Salomon S/LAB models.

expert_reviews.conclusion_excerpt: A lot of us are in the generation that truly believe that X is gon’ give it to ya. This X-Bionic Terraskin 03 is, sadly, an exception to that rule.

durability.evidence_excerpt: Based on the miles I logged, the outsole appears highly durable.

responsiveness.evidence_excerpt: It overpowered the inner midsole material to the point that it was hard to tell that a softer foam was in the mix.

fit_width.evidence_excerpt: The fit is kinda long, but if I went down in sizing, I feel like it would have created even more issues.

protection.evidence_excerpt: A thicker engineered mesh, lots of cushion in the collar, and a very structured heel counter make up the protection for your foot.

cushioning.evidence_excerpt: That same waffled design comes directly from the exoskeleton of the midsole called the SpeedFrame.

stability.evidence_excerpt: Uptop, the quality materials continue.

lightness.evidence_excerpt: That’s a lot for an experimental type of shoe.
